records.rationale: The only universe member whose query string contains punctuation, and the only one with a second listed share class. Two distinct risks compound: how the hyphen is tokenized, and which class the attention refers to.

Attention to Berkshire Hathaway is not class-specific in the way this ticker is.

records.rationale: Two independent problems. Lexically, 'GME' is a widely used US acronym for Graduate Medical Education. Substantively, this ticker carries a documented meme-driven retail-attention regime in which search spikes are generated by social-media dynamics unrelated to company information.
records.possible_unrelated_interpretation: 'GME' = Graduate Medical Education (residency and fellowship training, a common US institutional acronym); also an abbreviation of 'game'.
records.identifies_company_assessment: IDENTIFIES the issuer for most financial-context searches, but the ATTENTION IT MEASURES may be a different construct from the one the study intends. A z-score spike may index a social-media episode rather than information arrival about earnings. This is the clearest case in the universe where lexical uniqueness does not deliver construct validity.

unresolved_items: F5 is NOT closed. This audit is the offline half only.
No empirical comparison of candidate query forms has been performed, and none is authorized by this document.
BRK-B: how Google tokenizes the hyphen, and whether 'BRK-B' / 'BRK.B' / 'BRK/B' return materially different series, cannot be determined offline.
GOOGL: the magnitude of any leakage from 'google' mistypings cannot be estimated offline.
GME: whether the meme-driven attention regime constitutes a different construct from earnings-relevant information arrival is a substantive question no lexical screen can answer.

Google Trends 'topic' entities were NOT enumerated: doing so requires a live Trends suggestion call, which is prohibited here. Every proposed_alt_5_google_topic is therefore NONE_KNOWN_FROM_REPOSITORY_EVIDENCE.
Trends' own series-revision behaviour is undocumented in this repository and remains an open item under F5.
Any query change would require a dated methodology version and is NOT proposed here.
